title: Wild Animals I Have Known (Annotated)
author: ernest-thompson-seton
description:
Lobo knows where the traps are. Silverspot knows his flock and his country. Raggylug has much to learn, and Molly is determined that he shall live to learn it. Across eight stories, Ernest Thompson Seton follows animals whose particular gifts become clear when their lives are put to the test.

First published in 1898, *Wild Animals I Have Known* turns the animal encounter into an intimate portrait. A hunt changes the hunter's measure of success; a familiar dog unsettles easy judgments; a mother's persistence gives a small life extraordinary weight. Adventure and close observation lead the reader toward attachments that the endings do not always spare.

This AMBER SERIES edition from AETERNUS presents the English collection with new publisher illustrations, an author portrait, a glossary, and an afterword. Seton's original “Note to the Reader” accompanies the stories, explaining the individual lives and composed histories behind a book whose animals remain difficult to forget.

title: The Biography of a Grizzly (Annotated)
author: ernest-thompson-seton
description:
Wahb begins as a cub beside his mother, learning where to find food and when to take shelter. Alone, he must learn the rest from the country itself. Seasons pass, wounds leave their marks, and the small bear becomes a formidable presence whose strength seems equal to every rival. Yet strength, too, has its season.

In *The Biography of a Grizzly*, Ernest Thompson Seton follows one life through cubhood, power, and decline. The cliffs, streams, feeding grounds, and marked trees acquire a history as Wahb acquires his own. Every new encounter carries something of the encounters that came before, and the reader remembers the cub within the great bear.

This AMBER SERIES edition from AETERNUS presents the English book of 1900 with new publisher illustrations, an author portrait, a glossary, and an afterword. Brief, vivid, and deeply attentive to the passing of a life, it remains one of Seton's most concentrated animal narratives.

title: Lives of the Hunted (Annotated)
author: ernest-thompson-seton
description:
Two lambs, scarcely born, are already beyond a hunter's reach. A coyote learns from every narrow escape. A small dog discovers what it means to stand his ground. In eight stories, Ernest Thompson Seton follows animals whose lives depend on the exact use of strength, memory, and the country around them.

From Krag's mountain heights to a sparrow's street, *Lives of the Hunted* makes room for grandeur, mishap, devotion, and the hard education of experience. Johnny Bear, the mother teal, Chink, and Tito belong to a company whose smallest members can command the closest attention. Seton's original introductory note explains how observation and imagination meet in their histories.

This AMBER SERIES edition from AETERNUS presents the English collection of 1901 with new publisher illustrations, an author portrait, a glossary, and an afterword. The eight stories retain their distinct voices and their changing scale. Each opens another view of a world in which staying alive is an accomplishment with a history.

title: Animal Heroes (Annotated)
author: ernest-thompson-seton
description:
A gray cat learns the uses of an alley. A pigeon has a continent of dangers between himself and home. A little terrier faces an enemy no sensible measure of size would allow him to challenge. Seton's heroes announce themselves through what they do, often when nobody expects very much of them.

In eight stories, *Animal Heroes* follows gifts as different as speed, fidelity, cunning, and courage. Arnaux, Little Warhorse, Snap, and the wolves of the western country share the book with a lynx, a resourceful cat, and the White Reindeer of legend. Seton's opening note explains the observed lives and composite histories behind their adventures.

This AMBER SERIES edition from AETERNUS presents the English collection of 1905 with new publisher illustrations, an author portrait, a glossary, and an afterword. The stories move from the crowded street to the open country, asking the reader to look closely before deciding where greatness may be found.

title: Monarch, the Big Bear of Tallac (Annotated)
author: ernest-thompson-seton
description:
A small bear remembers honey and a familiar voice. Years later, the great bear of Tallac can break ropes, defeat traps, and send mounted men scrambling for safety. His strength has grown with his knowledge of the mountains. The people pursuing him have been learning too, and they are determined to take him alive.

Ernest Thompson Seton follows this contest from the mischief of cubhood to the terrible narrowness of a cage. The chapters move like a river, gathering force through obstacles toward the final “Landlocked.” In his original foreword, Seton explains the actual bears and gathered testimony behind his historical novel of bear life.

This AMBER SERIES edition from AETERNUS presents the English text of 1904 with new publisher illustrations, an author portrait, a glossary, and an afterword. Appetite, memory, courage, and loss give the mighty animal a history that cannot be measured by his strength alone. It is the history the hunter must finally remember.
